<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="American_origins_of_the_conflict">American origins of the conflict</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=France_in_the_American_Revolutionary_War&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: American origins of the conflict">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/American_Revolution" title="American Revolution">American Revolution</A></DIV>
<P>After its defeat in the <A href="/wiki/Seven_Years%27_War" title="Seven Years' War">Seven Years' War</A> in 1763, France lost its vast holdings in North America. Meanwhile, the American colonists and the British government began to fight over whether Parliament in London or the colonial assemblies had primary responsibility for taxation. As part of that conflict, the colonists organized the <A href="/wiki/Boston_Tea_Party" title="Boston Tea Party">Boston Tea Party</A> in response to a tax on tea. The British government responded by passing the <A href="/wiki/Intolerable_Acts" title="Intolerable Acts">Intolerable Acts</A>, which included the closing of Boston Harbor and the revocation of Massachusetts's colonial charter.<SUP id="cite_ref-Boston_Port_Act_1-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Boston_Port_Act-1">[1]</A></SUP> This conflict exacerbated tensions further. The ideological conflict escalated into open warfare in 1775, at which point the American patriots revolted against British rule. France, who had been rebuilding her Navy and other forces, saw this as an opportunity to seriously weaken her perennial enemy. <SUP id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2">[2]</A></SUP></P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="French_involvement">French involvement</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=France_in_the_American_Revolutionary_War&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: French involvement">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<DIV class="thumb tleft">
<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:%C3%89tienne-Fran%C3%A7ois_de_Choiseul.jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a3/%C3%89tienne-Fran%C3%A7ois_de_Choiseul.jpg/220px-%C3%89tienne-Fran%C3%A7ois_de_Choiseul.jpg" width="220" height="277" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a3/%C3%89tienne-Fran%C3%A7ois_de_Choiseul.jpg/330px-%C3%89tienne-Fran%C3%A7ois_de_Choiseul.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/a3/%C3%89tienne-Fran%C3%A7ois_de_Choiseul.jpg 2x" data-file-width="370" data-file-height="466" /></A>
<DIV class="thumbcaption">
<DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:%C3%89tienne-Fran%C3%A7ois_de_Choiseul.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>
<A href="/wiki/%C3%89tienne_Fran%C3%A7ois,_duc_de_Choiseul" title="Étienne François, duc de Choiseul">Choiseul</A> actively reorganized the French army and navy for a future war of revenge against Britain.</DIV>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<P>France bitterly resented its loss in the Seven Years' War and sought revenge. It also wanted to strategically weaken Britain. Following the <A href="/wiki/United_States_Declaration_of_Independence" title="United States Declaration of Independence">Declaration of Independence</A>, the <A href="/wiki/American_Revolution" title="American Revolution">American Revolution</A> was well received by both the general population and the aristocracy in France. The Revolution was perceived as the incarnation of the <A href="/wiki/Age_of_Enlightenment" title="Age of Enlightenment">Enlightenment Spirit</A> against the "English tyranny." <A href="/wiki/Benjamin_Franklin" title="Benjamin Franklin">Benjamin Franklin</A> traveled to France in December 1776 in order to rally the nation's support, and he was welcomed with great enthusiasm. At first, French support was covert: French agents sent the Patriots military aid (predominantly gunpowder) through a company called <I><A href="/wiki/Roderigue_Hortalez_and_Company" title="Roderigue Hortalez and Company">Rodrigue Hortalez et Compagnie</A></I>, beginning in the spring of 1776. Estimates place the percentage of French supplied arms to the Americans in the Saratoga campaign at up to 90%.<SUP id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-3">[3]</A></SUP> By 1777, over five million <I><A href="/wiki/French_livre" title="French livre">livres</A></I> of aid had been sent to the American rebels.</P>
<P>Motivated by the prospect of glory in battle or animated by the sincere ideals of liberty and republicanism, volunteers like <A href="/wiki/Pierre_Charles_L%27Enfant" title="Pierre Charles L'Enfant">Pierre Charles L'Enfant</A> joined the American army. The most famous was <A href="/wiki/Marquis_de_Lafayette" class="mw-redirect" title="Marquis de Lafayette">Lafayette</A>, a charming young aristocrat who defied the king's order and enlisted in 1777 at age 20. He became an aide to <A href="/wiki/George_Washington" title="George Washington">George Washington</A> and a combat general. More importantly, he solidified a favorable American view of France. Kramer argues that Lafayette provided a legitimacy for the war and confidence that there was serious European support for independence. Lafayette's personal style was highly attractive; the young man learned quickly, adapted to the <A href="/wiki/Patriot_(American_Revolution)" title="Patriot (American Revolution)">Patriot</A> style, avoided politics, and became a fast friend of General Washington. Fifty years later, after a major career in French politics, he returned as a beloved hero of the war.<SUP id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-4">[4]</A></SUP></P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Debate_over_quiet_aid_or_declaring_open_war">Debate over quiet aid or declaring open war</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=France_in_the_American_Revolutionary_War&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Debate over quiet aid or declaring open war">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<DIV class="thumb tright">
<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:D%27apr%C3%A8s_Jean-Marc_Nattier,_Portrait_de_Pierre-Augustin_Caron_de_Beaumarchais_(Biblioth%C3%A8que-mus%C3%A9e_de_la_Com%C3%A9die-Fran%C3%A7aise)_-001.jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/D%27apr%C3%A8s_Jean-Marc_Nattier%2C_Portrait_de_Pierre-Augustin_Caron_de_Beaumarchais_%28Biblioth%C3%A8que-mus%C3%A9e_de_la_Com%C3%A9die-Fran%C3%A7aise%29_-001.jpg/220px-D%27apr%C3%A8s_Jean-Marc_Nattier%2C_Portrait_de_Pierre-Augustin_Caron_de_Beaumarchais_%28Biblioth%C3%A8que-mus%C3%A9e_de_la_Com%C3%A9die-Fran%C3%A7aise%29_-001.jpg" width="220" height="284" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/D%27apr%C3%A8s_Jean-Marc_Nattier%2C_Portrait_de_Pierre-Augustin_Caron_de_Beaumarchais_%28Biblioth%C3%A8que-mus%C3%A9e_de_la_Com%C3%A9die-Fran%C3%A7aise%29_-001.jpg/330px-D%27apr%C3%A8s_Jean-Marc_Nattier%2C_Portrait_de_Pierre-Augustin_Caron_de_Beaumarchais_%28Biblioth%C3%A8que-mus%C3%A9e_de_la_Com%C3%A9die-Fran%C3%A7aise%29_-001.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/D%27apr%C3%A8s_Jean-Marc_Nattier%2C_Portrait_de_Pierre-Augustin_Caron_de_Beaumarchais_%28Biblioth%C3%A8que-mus%C3%A9e_de_la_Com%C3%A9die-Fran%C3%A7aise%29_-001.jpg/440px-D%27apr%C3%A8s_Jean-Marc_Nattier%2C_Portrait_de_Pierre-Augustin_Caron_de_Beaumarchais_%28Biblioth%C3%A8que-mus%C3%A9e_de_la_Com%C3%A9die-Fran%C3%A7aise%29_-001.jpg 2x" data-file-width="442" data-file-height="571" /></A>
<DIV class="thumbcaption">
<DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:D%27apr%C3%A8s_Jean-Marc_Nattier,_Portrait_de_Pierre-Augustin_Caron_de_Beaumarchais_(Biblioth%C3%A8que-mus%C3%A9e_de_la_Com%C3%A9die-Fran%C3%A7aise)_-001.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>
Before open war between France and Britain, <A href="/wiki/Pierre_Beaumarchais" title="Pierre Beaumarchais">Pierre Beaumarchais</A> was at the center of an <A href="/wiki/Arms_traffic" class="mw-redirect" title="Arms traffic">arms traffic</A> to support American Insurgents.</DIV>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<P>Up against the British power, the young nation lacked arms and allies, and so it turned towards France. France was not directly interested in the conflict, but saw it as an opportunity to contest British power by supporting a new British opponent. Through negotiations conducted first by <A href="/wiki/Silas_Deane" title="Silas Deane">Silas Deane</A> and then by <A href="/wiki/Benjamin_Franklin" title="Benjamin Franklin">Benjamin Franklin</A>, France began covert support of the American cause.</P>
<P>Secretly approached by <A href="/wiki/Louis_XVI_of_France" title="Louis XVI of France">Louis XVI</A> and France's <A href="/wiki/Foreign_Minister" class="mw-redirect" title="Foreign Minister">foreign minister</A>, the <A href="/wiki/Charles_Gravier,_comte_de_Vergennes" title="Charles Gravier, comte de Vergennes">comte de Vergennes</A>, <A href="/wiki/Pierre_Beaumarchais" title="Pierre Beaumarchais">Pierre Beaumarchais</A> was authorized to sell gunpowder and ammunition to the Americans for close to a million <A href="/wiki/Livre_tournois" title="Livre tournois">pounds</A> under the veil of the French company <I>Rodrigue Hortalez et Compagnie</I>. The aid given by France, much of which passed through the neutral <A href="/wiki/Dutch_Republic" title="Dutch Republic">Dutch</A> West Indies port of <A href="/wiki/Sint_Eustatius" title="Sint Eustatius">Sint Eustatius</A>, contributed to <A href="/wiki/George_Washington" title="George Washington">George Washington</A>'s survival against the British onslaught in 1776 and 1777. The aid was also a major factor in the defeat of General Burgoyne's expedition in the Champlain corridor that ended in a British disaster at Saratoga. French ports accommodated American ships, including <A href="/wiki/Privateer" title="Privateer">privateers</A> and <A href="/wiki/Continental_Navy" title="Continental Navy">Continental Navy</A> warships, that acted against British merchant ships. France provided significant economic aid, either as donations or loans, and also offered technical assistance, granting some of its military strategists "vacations" so they could assist American troops.</P>
<P><A href="/wiki/Silas_Deane" title="Silas Deane">Silas Deane</A>, appointed by the Americans and helped by French animosity towards Britain, obtained unofficial aid, starting in early 1776. However, the goal was the total involvement of France in the war. A new delegation composed of <A href="/wiki/Benjamin_Franklin" title="Benjamin Franklin">Franklin</A>, Deane, and <A href="/wiki/Arthur_Lee_(diplomat)" title="Arthur Lee (diplomat)">Arthur Lee</A>, was appointed to lobby for the involvement of European nations. Franklin, age 70 and already well known in French intellectual circles for his scientific discoveries, served as the chief diplomat with the title of "minister" (the term "ambassador" was not used). He dressed in rough frontier clothes rather than formal court dress, and met with many leading diplomats, aristocrats, intellectuals, scientists and financiers. Franklin's image and writings caught the French imagination – there were many images of him sold on the market – and he became the image of the archetypal new American and a hero for aspirations for a new order inside France. When the international climate at the end of 1777 had become tenser, <A href="/wiki/Habsburg_Monarchy" title="Habsburg Monarchy">Habsburg Austria</A> requested the support of France in the <A href="/wiki/War_of_the_Bavarian_Succession" title="War of the Bavarian Succession">War of the Bavarian Succession</A> against the <A href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Prussia" title="Kingdom of Prussia">Prussia</A> in line with the <A href="/wiki/Franco-Austrian_Alliance" title="Franco-Austrian Alliance">Franco-Austrian Alliance</A>. France refused, causing the relationship with Austria to turn sour. Under these conditions, asking <A href="/wiki/Austria" title="Austria">Austria</A> to assist France in a war against the British was impossible. Attempts to rally <A href="/wiki/Spain" title="Spain">Spain</A> also failed: Spain did not immediately recognize potential gains, and the American revolutionary spirit was seen as threatening the legitimacy of the Spanish Crown in its own American <A href="/wiki/Spanish_colonization_of_the_Americas" title="Spanish colonization of the Americas">colonies</A>.</P>
<P>Public opinion in France was in favor of open war, but King Louis and his advisors were reluctant due to the possible risks and heavy expenses involved. The king's economic and military advisors, in particular, remained reluctant. The <A href="/wiki/French_Navy" title="French Navy">French Navy</A> was being rapidly rebuilt, but there were doubts as to how ready it was for serious conflict. Financiers <A href="/wiki/Anne_Robert_Jacques_Turgot,_Baron_de_Laune" class="mw-redirect" title="Anne Robert Jacques Turgot, Baron de Laune">Turgot</A> and <A href="/wiki/Jacques_Necker" title="Jacques Necker">Necker</A> warned war would be very expensive for France's wobbly system of taxation and finance.</P>
<P>The Americans argued that an alliance of the United States, France, and Spain would assure a rapid defeat of the British, but Vergennes, waiting until his navy was ready, hesitated. On July 23, 1777, Vergennes decided that it was time to decide either total assistance, with war, or abandonment of the new nation. The choice, ratified by the king, was war.<SUP id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-5">[5]</A></SUP></P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Entry_into_the_war">Entry into the war</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=France_in_the_American_Revolutionary_War&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Entry into the war">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/Franco-American_alliance" title="Franco-American alliance">Franco-American alliance</A></DIV>
<DIV class="thumb tright">
<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Surrender_of_General_Burgoyne.jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/71/Surrender_of_General_Burgoyne.jpg/220px-Surrender_of_General_Burgoyne.jpg" width="220" height="146" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/71/Surrender_of_General_Burgoyne.jpg/330px-Surrender_of_General_Burgoyne.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/71/Surrender_of_General_Burgoyne.jpg/440px-Surrender_of_General_Burgoyne.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3000" data-file-height="1987" /></A>
<DIV class="thumbcaption">
<DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Surrender_of_General_Burgoyne.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>
<I>Surrender of General Burgoyne</I> at the <A href="/wiki/Battle_of_Saratoga" class="mw-redirect" title="Battle of Saratoga">Battle of Saratoga</A>, by <A href="/wiki/John_Trumbull" title="John Trumbull">John Trumbull</A>, 1822</DIV>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<P>The British had taken <A href="/wiki/Philadelphia" title="Philadelphia">Philadelphia</A> in 1777, but American victory at the <A href="/wiki/Battle_of_Saratoga" class="mw-redirect" title="Battle of Saratoga">Battle of Saratoga</A> brought back hope to the <A href="/wiki/Patriot_(American_Revolution)" title="Patriot (American Revolution)">Patriots</A> and enthusiasm in France. The army of <A href="/wiki/John_Burgoyne" title="John Burgoyne">Burgoyne</A> surrendered to American forces after <A href="/wiki/Battle_of_Saratoga" class="mw-redirect" title="Battle of Saratoga">Saratoga</A> and France realized that the United States could be victorious. The king directed Vergennes to negotiate an alliance with the Americans.<SUP id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-6">[6]</A></SUP></P>
<P>France formally recognized the United States on February 6, 1778, with the signing of the <A href="/wiki/Treaty_of_Alliance_(1778)" title="Treaty of Alliance (1778)">Treaty of Alliance</A>. Hostilities soon followed after Britain declared war on France on March 17, 1778. The British naval force, then the largest fleet afloat, and French fleet confronted each other from the beginning. The British avoided intercepting a French fleet that left <A href="/wiki/Toulon" title="Toulon">Toulon</A> under <A href="/wiki/Charles_Hector,_comte_d%27Estaing" class="mw-redirect" title="Charles Hector, comte d'Estaing">the comte d'Estaing</A> in April for North America, fearing the French fleet at <A href="/wiki/Brest,_France" title="Brest, France">Brest</A> might then be used to launch an invasion of Britain. France had kept the Brest fleet to protect commercial shipping in European waters, and it sailed out only after a British fleet was confirmed to have left in pursuit of d'Estaing, thus weakening the British Channel fleet. In spite of this reduction, the British fleet still outnumbered the French fleet at Brest, and Admiral d'Orvilliers was instructed to avoid combat when he sailed in July. D'Orvilliers met the fleet of Admiral <A href="/wiki/Augustus_Keppel,_1st_Viscount_Keppel" title="Augustus Keppel, 1st Viscount Keppel">Augustus Keppel</A> in the indecisive <A href="/wiki/Battle_of_Ushant_(1778)" title="Battle of Ushant (1778)">Battle of Ushant</A> on July 27, after which both fleets returned to port for repairs.</P>
<P>France did consider the landing of 40,000 men in the nearby British Isles but abandoned the idea because of logistical issues. On the continent, France was protected through its alliance with Austria which, even if it did not take part in the American Revolutionary War, affirmed its diplomatic support of France.</P>
<P>Other nations in Europe at first refused to openly join the war but both Spain and the <A href="/wiki/Dutch_Republic" title="Dutch Republic">Dutch Republic</A> gave unofficial support to the American cause. Vergennes was able to convince the Spanish to formally enter the war in 1779 and, in 1780, Britain <A href="/wiki/Fourth_Anglo-Dutch_War" title="Fourth Anglo-Dutch War">declared war</A> on the Dutch Republic over claims of Dutch violations of neutrality.</P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="North_American_operations">North American operations</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=France_in_the_American_Revolutionary_War&action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section: North American operations">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<DIV class="thumb tright">
<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:W-RSimpleMap.gif" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/W-RSimpleMap.gif/220px-W-RSimpleMap.gif" width="220" height="305" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/W-RSimpleMap.gif/330px-W-RSimpleMap.gif 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/W-RSimpleMap.gif/440px-W-RSimpleMap.gif 2x" data-file-width="1960" data-file-height="2718" /></A>
<DIV class="thumbcaption">
<DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:W-RSimpleMap.gif" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>
Franco-American routes during the <A href="/wiki/Yorktown_campaign" title="Yorktown campaign">Yorktown campaign</A>.</DIV>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<P>French participation in North America was initially maritime in nature and marked by some indecision on the part of its military leaders. In 1778, American and French planners organized an attempt to capture <A href="/wiki/Newport,_Rhode_Island" title="Newport, Rhode Island">Newport, Rhode Island</A>, then under British occupation. <A href="/wiki/Battle_of_Rhode_Island" title="Battle of Rhode Island">The attempt failed</A>, in part because Admiral d'Estaing did not land French troops prior to sailing out of <A href="/wiki/Narragansett_Bay" title="Narragansett Bay">Narragansett Bay</A> to meet the British fleet. He then sailed to <A href="/wiki/Boston" title="Boston">Boston</A> after his fleet was damaged in a storm. In 1779, d'Estaing again led his fleet to North America for joint operations, this time against British-held <A href="/wiki/Savannah,_Georgia" title="Savannah, Georgia">Savannah, Georgia</A>. About 3,000 French joined with 2,000 Americans in the <A href="/wiki/Siege_of_Savannah" title="Siege of Savannah">Siege of Savannah</A>, in which a naval bombardment was unsuccessful. An attempted assault of the entrenched British position was repulsed with heavy losses.</P>
<P>Support became more notable when, in 1780, 6,000 soldiers led by <A href="/wiki/Jean-Baptiste_Donatien_de_Vimeur,_comte_de_Rochambeau" title="Jean-Baptiste Donatien de Vimeur, comte de Rochambeau">Rochambeau</A> landed at Newport, itself abandoned in 1779 by the British, and then established a naval base there. These forces were largely inactive since the fleet was closely watched by the British fleet from its bases in New York and eastern <A href="/wiki/Long_Island" title="Long Island">Long Island</A>. By early 1781, with the war dragging on, French military planners were finally convinced that more significant operations would be required in North America to bring a decisive end to the war. That year's West Indies fleet was commanded by <A href="/wiki/Fran%C3%A7ois_Joseph_Paul_de_Grasse" title="François Joseph Paul de Grasse">the comte de Grasse</A>, and specific arrangements were made to coordinate operations with him. De Grasse asked to be supplied with North American pilots and to be informed of possible operations in North America to which he might contribute. Rochambeau and Washington met in <A href="/wiki/Wethersfield,_Connecticut" title="Wethersfield, Connecticut">Wethersfield, Connecticut</A> in May 1781 to discuss their options. Washington wanted to drive the British from both New York City and <A href="/wiki/Virginia" title="Virginia">Virginia</A> (the latter led first by <A href="/wiki/Benedict_Arnold" title="Benedict Arnold">Benedict Arnold</A>, then by Brigadier <A href="/wiki/William_Phillips_(British_Army_officer)" title="William Phillips (British Army officer)">William Phillips</A> and eventually by <A href="/wiki/Charles_Cornwallis,_1st_Marquess_Cornwallis" title="Charles Cornwallis, 1st Marquess Cornwallis">Charles Cornwallis</A>). Virginia was also seen as a potent threat that could be fought with naval assistance. These two options were dispatched to the Caribbean along with the requested pilots. Rochambeau, in a separate letter, urged de Grasse to come to the <A href="/wiki/Chesapeake_Bay" title="Chesapeake Bay">Chesapeake Bay</A> for operations in Virginia. Following the Wethersfield conference, Rochambeau moved his army to <A href="/wiki/White_Plains,_New_York" title="White Plains, New York">White Plains, New York</A> and placed his command under Washington.</P>
<P>De Grasse received these letters in July at roughly the same time Cornwallis was preparing to occupy <A href="/wiki/Yorktown,_Virginia" title="Yorktown, Virginia">Yorktown, Virginia</A>. De Grasse concurred with Rochambeau and subsequently sent a dispatch indicating that he would reach the Chesapeake at the end of August but that agreements with the Spanish meant he could only stay until mid-October. The arrival of his dispatches prompted the Franco-American army to begin a march for Virginia. De Grasse reached the Chesapeake as planned and his troops were sent to assist Lafayette's army in the blockade of Cornwallis's army. A British fleet sent to confront de Grasse's control of the Chesapeake was defeated by the French on September 5 at the <A href="/wiki/Battle_of_the_Chesapeake" title="Battle of the Chesapeake">Battle of the Chesapeake</A> and the Newport fleet delivered the French siege train to complete the allied military arrival. The <A href="/wiki/Siege_of_Yorktown" title="Siege of Yorktown">Siege of Yorktown</A> and following surrender by Cornwallis on October 19 were decisive in ending major hostilities in North America.<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP></P>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Other_theaters">Other theaters</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=France_in_the_American_Revolutionary_War&action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section: Other theaters">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<DIV class="thumb tright">
<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Prise_La_Grenade_juillet_1779.jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/Prise_La_Grenade_juillet_1779.jpg/220px-Prise_La_Grenade_juillet_1779.jpg" width="220" height="225" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/Prise_La_Grenade_juillet_1779.jpg/330px-Prise_La_Grenade_juillet_1779.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/Prise_La_Grenade_juillet_1779.jpg/440px-Prise_La_Grenade_juillet_1779.jpg 2x" data-file-width="626" data-file-height="640" /></A>

The capture of the island of <A href="/wiki/Grenada" title="Grenada">Grenada</A> by the troops of <A href="/wiki/Charles_Hector,_comte_d%27Estaing" class="mw-redirect" title="Charles Hector, comte d'Estaing">D'Estaing</A>.</DIV>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<P>Other important battles between the French and the British were spaced out around the world, from the West Indies to India. France's navy at first dominated in the West Indies, capturing <A href="/wiki/Invasion_of_Dominica_(1778)" title="Invasion of Dominica (1778)">Dominica</A>, <A href="/wiki/Battle_of_Grenada" title="Battle of Grenada">Grenada</A>, <A href="/wiki/Capture_of_Saint_Vincent" title="Capture of Saint Vincent">Saint Vincent</A>, <A href="/wiki/Capture_of_Montserrat" title="Capture of Montserrat">Montserrat</A>, <A href="/wiki/Invasion_of_Tobago" title="Invasion of Tobago">Tobago</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Battle_of_Saint_Kitts" title="Battle of Saint Kitts">St. Kitts</A>, but losing <A href="/wiki/Battle_of_St._Lucia" title="Battle of St. Lucia">St. Lucia</A> at the beginning of the war. A planned Franco-Spanish invasion of <A href="/wiki/Jamaica" title="Jamaica">Jamaica</A> was aborted after the decisive <A href="/wiki/Battle_of_the_Saintes" title="Battle of the Saintes">Battle of the Saintes</A> in 1782. At the end of the war. the French <A href="/wiki/Capture_of_the_Turks_and_Caicos_Islands" class="mw-redirect" title="Capture of the Turks and Caicos Islands">captured the Turks and Caicos Islands</A>. In European waters, France and Spain joined forces with the entry of Spain into the war in 1779. An <A href="/wiki/Armada_of_1779" title="Armada of 1779">attempted invasion of Britain</A> failed due to a variety of factors. French and Spanish forces <A href="/wiki/Great_Siege_of_Gibraltar" title="Great Siege of Gibraltar">besieged Gibraltar</A> from 1779 to 1783, but were unsuccessful in either storming the site, or preventing repeated British relief of its garrison. They were more successful in <A href="/wiki/Invasion_of_Minorca,_1781" class="mw-redirect" title="Invasion of Minorca, 1781">capturing Minorca</A> in Europe and <A href="/wiki/Capture_of_Demerara_and_Essequibo" title="Capture of Demerara and Essequibo">Demerara and Essequibo</A> in South America in February 1782.</P>
<P>In <A href="/wiki/India" title="India">India</A>, British troops gained control of French outposts in 1778 and 1779, sparking the <A href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Mysore" title="Kingdom of Mysore">Kingdom of Mysore</A>, a longtime French ally, to begin the <A href="/wiki/Second_Anglo-Mysore_War" title="Second Anglo-Mysore War">Second Anglo-Mysore War</A>. Allied with the French, the Mysoreans for a time threatened British positions on the east coast, but that war ended <I><A href="/wiki/Status_quo_ante_bellum" title="Status quo ante bellum">status quo ante bellum</A></I> in 1784. A French fleet commanded by the <A href="/wiki/Pierre_Andr%C3%A9_de_Suffren_de_Saint_Tropez" class="mw-redirect" title="Pierre André de Suffren de Saint Tropez">Bailli de Suffren</A> fought a series of largely inconclusive battles with a British fleet under <A href="/wiki/Edward_Hughes_(admiral)" class="mw-redirect" title="Edward Hughes (admiral)">Sir Edward Hughes</A>, and the only major military land action, the 1783 <A href="/wiki/Siege_of_Cuddalore" title="Siege of Cuddalore">Siege of Cuddalore</A>, was cut short by news that a preliminary peace had been signed.</P>
<P>Because of decisive battles on American soil, the French were in a strong position during the <A href="/wiki/Treaty_of_Paris_(1783)" title="Treaty of Paris (1783)">peace negotiations in Paris</A>.</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Peace_and_consequences">Peace and consequences</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=France_in_the_American_Revolutionary_War&action=edit&section=7" title="Edit section: Peace and consequences">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>Starting with the Siege of Yorktown, Benjamin Franklin never informed France of the secret negotiations that took place directly between Britain and the United States. Britain acknowledged that the United States owned all the land south of the <A href="/wiki/Great_Lakes" title="Great Lakes">Great Lakes</A> and east of the <A href="/wiki/Mississippi_River" title="Mississippi River">Mississippi River</A>, except for Florida (which went to Spain). However, since France was not included in the American-British peace discussions, the alliance between France and the U.S. was weakened. Thus the influence of France and Spain in future negotiations was limited.<SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[8]</A></SUP></P>
<DIV class="thumb tright">
<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Treaty_of_Paris_by_Benjamin_West_1783.jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fe/Treaty_of_Paris_by_Benjamin_West_1783.jpg/220px-Treaty_of_Paris_by_Benjamin_West_1783.jpg" width="220" height="165" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fe/Treaty_of_Paris_by_Benjamin_West_1783.jpg/330px-Treaty_of_Paris_by_Benjamin_West_1783.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fe/Treaty_of_Paris_by_Benjamin_West_1783.jpg/440px-Treaty_of_Paris_by_Benjamin_West_1783.jpg 2x" data-file-width="500" data-file-height="375" /></A>
<DIV class="thumbcaption">
<DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Treaty_of_Paris_by_Benjamin_West_1783.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>
Ratification of the <A href="/wiki/Treaty_of_Paris_(1783)" title="Treaty of Paris (1783)">Treaty of Paris</A>, 1783. The British delegation refused to pose for the picture</DIV>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<P>The war formally ended in September 1783 with the signing of the <A href="/wiki/Treaty_of_Paris_(1783)" title="Treaty of Paris (1783)">Treaty of Paris</A>. France gained (or regained) territories in the <A href="/wiki/Americas" title="Americas">Americas</A>, <A href="/wiki/Africa" title="Africa">Africa</A>, and <A href="/wiki/India" title="India">India</A>. Losses in the <A href="/wiki/Treaty_of_Paris_(1763)" title="Treaty of Paris (1763)">1763 Treaty of Paris</A> and in the <A href="/wiki/Treaty_of_Utrecht" title="Treaty of Utrecht">Treaty of Utrecht</A> (1713) were in part regained: <A href="/wiki/Tobago" title="Tobago">Tobago</A>, <A href="/wiki/Saint_Lucia" title="Saint Lucia">Saint Lucia</A>, the <A href="/wiki/Senegal_River" title="Senegal River">Senegal River</A> area, as well as increased fishing rights in <A href="/wiki/Newfoundland_(island)" title="Newfoundland (island)">Terra Nova</A>. Spain regained <A href="/wiki/Spanish_Florida" title="Spanish Florida">Florida</A> and <A href="/wiki/Minorca" class="mw-redirect" title="Minorca">Minorca</A>, but <A href="/wiki/Gibraltar" title="Gibraltar">Gibraltar</A> remained in the hands of the British.</P>
<P>Because the French involvement in the war was distant and naval in nature, over a billion <A href="/wiki/Livre_tournois" title="Livre tournois">livres tournois</A> were spent by the French government to support the war effort, raising its overall debt to about 3.315 billion. The finances of the French state were in disastrous shape and were made worse by <A href="/wiki/Jacques_Necker" title="Jacques Necker">Jacques Necker</A>, who, rather than increase taxes, used loans to pay off debts. State secretary of Finances <A href="/wiki/Charles_Alexandre_de_Calonne" title="Charles Alexandre de Calonne">Charles Alexandre de Calonne</A> attempted to fix the deficit problem by asking for the taxation of the property of nobles and clergy but was dismissed and exiled for his ideas. The French instability further weakened the reforms that were essential in the re-establishment of stable French finances. Trade also severely declined during the war, but was revived by 1783.</P>
<P>The war was especially important for the prestige and pride of France, who was reinstated in the role of European arbiter. However, Great Britain, not France, became the leading trading partner of the United States.<SUP id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-9">[9]</A></SUP> The French took pride in their cultural influence on the young country through the <A href="/wiki/Age_of_Enlightenment" title="Age of Enlightenment">Enlightenment</A>, as attested by Franklin and Jefferson, and as embodied in the Declaration of Independence in 1776 and the <A href="/wiki/United_States_Constitution" title="United States Constitution">United States Constitution</A> in 1787. In turn, the Revolution influenced France.<SUP id="cite_ref-10" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-10">[10]</A></SUP> <A href="/wiki/Liberalism" title="Liberalism">Liberal</A> elites were satisfied by the victory but there were also some major consequences. European <A href="/wiki/Conservatism" title="Conservatism">conservative</A> Royalists and nobility had become nervous, and began to take measures in order to secure their positions. On May 22, 1781, the <A href="/wiki/Decree_of_S%C3%A9gur" class="mw-redirect" title="Decree of Ségur">Decree of Ségur</A> closed the military post offices of the upper rank to the common persons, reserving those ranks exclusively for the nobility.</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Financial_aspects">Financial aspects</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=France_in_the_American_Revolutionary_War&action=edit&section=8" title="Edit section: Financial aspects">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>In all the French spent 1.3 billion livres to support the Americans directly, in addition to the money it spent fighting Britain on land and sea outside the U.S.<SUP id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-11">[11]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-12" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-12">[12]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-13" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-13">[13]</A></SUP></P>
<P>France's status as a great modern power was re-affirmed by the war, but it was detrimental to the country's finances. Even though France's European territories were not affected, victory in a war against Great Britain with battles like the decisive <A href="/wiki/Siege_of_Yorktown" title="Siege of Yorktown">siege of Yorktown</A> in 1781 had a large financial cost which severely degraded fragile finances and increased the national debt. France gained little except that it weakened its main strategic enemy and gained a new, fast-growing ally that could become a welcome trading partner. However, the trade never materialized, and in 1793 the United States proclaimed its neutrality in the war between Great Britain and the French Republic.<SUP id="cite_ref-14" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-14">[14]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Some historians argue that France primarily sought revenge against Great Britain for the loss of territory in North America and India from the previous conflict. But Jonathan R. Dull states that France intervened because of dispassionate calculation, not because of <A href="/wiki/Anglophobia" title="Anglophobia">Anglophobia</A> or a desire to avenge the loss of Canada.<SUP id="cite_ref-15" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-15">[15]</A></SUP></P>

<P><I><B>The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring</B></I> is a 2001 <A href="/wiki/Epic_film" title="Epic film">epic</A> <A href="/wiki/Adventure_film" title="Adventure film">adventure</A> <A href="/wiki/Fantasy_film" title="Fantasy film">fantasy film</A> directed by <A href="/wiki/Peter_Jackson" title="Peter Jackson">Peter Jackson</A> based on the <A href="/wiki/The_Fellowship_of_the_Ring" title="The Fellowship of the Ring">first volume</A> of <A href="/wiki/J._R._R._Tolkien" title="J. R. R. Tolkien">J. R. R. Tolkien</A>'s <I><A href="/wiki/The_Lord_of_the_Rings" title="The Lord of the Rings">The Lord of the Rings</A></I> (1954–1955).<SUP id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-4">[4]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-5">[5]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-6">[6]</A></SUP> It is the first instalment in <I><A href="/wiki/The_Lord_of_the_Rings_(film_series)" title="The Lord of the Rings (film series)">The Lord of the Rings series</A></I>, and was followed by <I><A href="/wiki/The_Lord_of_the_Rings:_The_Two_Towers" title="The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers">The Two Towers</A></I> (2002) and <I><A href="/wiki/The_Lord_of_the_Rings:_The_Return_of_the_King" title="The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King">The Return of the King</A></I> (2003), based on the second and third volumes of <I>The Lord of the Rings</I>.</P>
<P>Set in <A href="/wiki/Middle-earth" title="Middle-earth">Middle-earth</A>, the story tells of the Dark Lord <A href="/wiki/Sauron" title="Sauron">Sauron</A> (<A href="/wiki/Sala_Baker" title="Sala Baker">Sala Baker</A>), who is seeking the <A href="/wiki/One_Ring" title="One Ring">One Ring</A>. The Ring has found its way to the young <A href="/wiki/Hobbit" title="Hobbit">hobbit</A> <A href="/wiki/Frodo_Baggins" title="Frodo Baggins">Frodo Baggins</A> (<A href="/wiki/Elijah_Wood" title="Elijah Wood">Elijah Wood</A>). The fate of Middle-earth hangs in the balance as Frodo and eight companions who form the <A href="/wiki/Fellowship_of_the_Ring_(characters)" class="mw-redirect" title="Fellowship of the Ring (characters)">Fellowship of the Ring</A> begin their journey to <A href="/wiki/Mount_Doom" title="Mount Doom">Mount Doom</A> in the land of <A href="/wiki/Mordor" title="Mordor">Mordor</A>, the only place where the Ring can be destroyed.</P>
<P>Released on 10 December 2001, the film was highly acclaimed by critics and fans alike who considered it to be a landmark in film-making and an achievement in the fantasy film genre. It has continued to be featured on critic lists of the <A href="/wiki/List_of_films_considered_the_best" title="List of films considered the best">greatest fantasy films ever made</A>, as of 2017<SUP class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><A class="external text" href="//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Lord_of_the_Rings:_The_Fellowship_of_the_Ring&action=edit">[update]</A></SUP>. The film earned over $871 million worldwide and became the second highest-grossing film of 2001 in the US and worldwide (behind <I><A href="/wiki/Harry_Potter_and_the_Philosopher%27s_Stone_(film)" title="Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (film)">Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone</A></I>).</P>
<P>It was nominated for thirteen <A href="/wiki/Academy_Awards" title="Academy Awards">Oscars</A> at the <A href="/wiki/74th_Academy_Awards" title="74th Academy Awards">74th Academy Awards</A> ceremony, including <A href="/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture" title="Academy Award for Best Picture">Best Picture</A>, <A href="/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Director" title="Academy Award for Best Director">Best Director</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor" title="Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor">Best Supporting Actor</A> for McKellen, winning four for <A href="/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Cinematography" title="Academy Award for Best Cinematography">Best Cinematography</A>, <A href="/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Makeup" class="mw-redirect" title="Academy Award for Best Makeup">Best Makeup</A>, <A href="/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Original_Score" title="Academy Award for Best Original Score">Best Original Score</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Visual_Effects" title="Academy Award for Best Visual Effects">Best Visual Effects</A>. It also won four <A href="/wiki/British_Academy_Film_Awards" title="British Academy Film Awards">British Academy Film Awards</A>, including Best Film and Best Director BAFTA awards. The <I>Special Extended Edition</I> was released to DVD on 12 November 2002 and to <A href="/wiki/Blu-ray_Disc" class="mw-redirect" title="Blu-ray Disc">Blu-ray Disc</A> on 28 June 2011. In 2007, <I>The Fellowship of the Ring</I> was voted <ABBR title="Number">No.</ABBR> 50 on the <A href="/wiki/American_Film_Institute" title="American Film Institute">American Film Institute</A>'s list of <A href="/wiki/AFI%27s_100_Years...100_Movies_(10th_Anniversary_Edition)" title="AFI's 100 Years...100 Movies (10th Anniversary Edition)">100 greatest American films</A>. The AFI also voted it the second greatest fantasy film of all time during their <A href="/wiki/AFI%27s_10_Top_10" title="AFI's 10 Top 10">10 Top 10</A> special. The film ranks #24 on <A href="/wiki/Empire_magazine" class="mw-redirect" title="Empire magazine"><I>Empire</I></A>'s 2008 list of the 500 greatest movies of all time.<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP></P>

<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Plot">Plot</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Lord_of_the_Rings:_The_Fellowship_of_the_Ring&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Plot">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<P>In the Second Age of <A href="/wiki/Middle-earth" title="Middle-earth">Middle-earth</A>, the lords of <A href="/wiki/Elf_(Middle-earth)" title="Elf (Middle-earth)">Elves</A>, <A href="/wiki/Dwarf_(Middle-earth)" title="Dwarf (Middle-earth)">Dwarves</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Man_(Middle-earth)" title="Man (Middle-earth)">Men</A> are given <A href="/wiki/Rings_of_Power" title="Rings of Power">Rings of Power</A>. Unbeknownst to them, the <A href="/wiki/Sauron" title="Sauron">Dark Lord Sauron</A> forges the <A href="/wiki/One_Ring" title="One Ring">One Ring</A> in <A href="/wiki/Mount_Doom" title="Mount Doom">Mount Doom</A>, infusing into it a great part of his power to dominate, through it and at a distance, the other Rings, so he might conquer Middle-earth. A final alliance of men and elves battles Sauron’s forces in <A href="/wiki/Mordor" title="Mordor">Mordor</A>, where Prince <A href="/wiki/Isildur" title="Isildur">Isildur</A> of <A href="/wiki/Gondor" title="Gondor">Gondor</A> severs Sauron's finger, and the Ring with it, thereby destroying his physical form. Unfortunately, the Ring's influence corrupts Isildur, and, rather than destroy the Ring, Isildur takes it for himself. Isildur is later killed by <A href="/wiki/Orc_(Middle-earth)" title="Orc (Middle-earth)">Orcs</A>, and the Ring is lost for 2,500 years, until it is found by <A href="/wiki/Gollum" title="Gollum">Gollum</A>, who owns it for five centuries. The Ring is then found by a <A href="/wiki/Hobbit" title="Hobbit">Hobbit</A> named <A href="/wiki/Bilbo_Baggins" title="Bilbo Baggins">Bilbo Baggins</A>.</P>
<P>Sixty years later, Bilbo celebrates his 111th birthday in the <A href="/wiki/Shire_(Middle-earth)" title="Shire (Middle-earth)">Shire</A>, reuniting with his old friend, <A href="/wiki/Gandalf" title="Gandalf">Gandalf the Grey</A>. Bilbo reveals that he intends to leave the Shire for one last adventure, and he leaves his inheritance, including the Ring, to his nephew, <A href="/wiki/Frodo_Baggins" title="Frodo Baggins">Frodo</A>. Although Bilbo has begun to become corrupted by the Ring and tries to keep it for himself, Gandalf intervenes. Gandalf, suspicious of the Ring, tells Frodo to keep it secret and to keep it safe. Gandalf then investigates the Ring, discovers its true identity, and returns to warn Frodo. Gandalf also learns that Gollum was tortured by Orcs, and that Gollum uttered two words during his torture: "Shire" and "Baggins." Gandalf instructs Frodo to leave the Shire, accompanied by his gardener <A href="/wiki/Samwise_Gamgee" title="Samwise Gamgee">Samwise Gamgee</A>. Gandalf rides to <A href="/wiki/Isengard" title="Isengard">Isengard</A> to meet with fellow wizard <A href="/wiki/Saruman" title="Saruman">Saruman</A> the White, but learns that he has joined forces with Sauron, who has unleashed the <A href="/wiki/Ringwraith" class="mw-redirect" title="Ringwraith">Ringwraiths</A> to find Frodo. After a brief battle, Saruman imprisons Gandalf. Frodo and Sam are joined by fellow Hobbits, <A href="/wiki/Meriadoc_Brandybuck" title="Meriadoc Brandybuck">Merry</A> and <A href="/wiki/Peregrin_Took" title="Peregrin Took">Pippin</A>, and they evade the Ringwraiths, arriving in <A href="/wiki/Bree_(Middle-earth)" title="Bree (Middle-earth)">Bree</A>, where they are meant to meet Gandalf. However, Gandalf never arrived, and they are instead aided by a ranger named <A href="/wiki/Aragorn" title="Aragorn">Strider</A>, a friend of Gandalf's, who escorts them to <A href="/wiki/Rivendell" title="Rivendell">Rivendell</A>.</P>
<P>The Hobbits are ambushed by the Ringwraiths, and one stabs Frodo with a cursed <A href="/wiki/Morgul_blade" class="mw-redirect" title="Morgul blade">Morgul blade</A>. <A href="/wiki/Arwen" title="Arwen">Arwen</A>, an elf and Strider’s lover, comes to Frodo’s aid and successfully takes him to Rivendell, where he is healed. Frodo meets Gandalf, who escaped Isengard on the back of a giant <A href="/wiki/Eagle_(Middle-earth)" title="Eagle (Middle-earth)">Eagle</A>. Arwen’s father, <A href="/wiki/Elrond" title="Elrond">Lord Elrond,</A> holds a council that decides the Ring must be destroyed in Mount Doom. While the members argue, Frodo volunteers to take the Ring, accompanied by Gandalf, Sam, Merry, Pippin, elf <A href="/wiki/Legolas" title="Legolas">Legolas</A>, dwarf <A href="/wiki/Gimli_(Middle-earth)" title="Gimli (Middle-earth)">Gimli</A>, <A href="/wiki/Boromir" title="Boromir">Boromir</A> of Gondor, and Strider, who is revealed to be Aragorn, Isildur’s heir and the rightful King of Gondor. Bilbo gives Frodo his sword, Sting. The Fellowship of the Ring sets off, but Saruman’s magic forces them to travel through the Mines of <A href="/wiki/Moria_(Middle-earth)" title="Moria (Middle-earth)">Moria</A>, much to Gandalf's displeasure.</P>
<P>The Fellowship discovers that the dwarves within Moria have been slain, and they are attacked by Orcs and a cave <A href="/wiki/Troll" title="Troll">troll</A>. They defeat them, but are confronted by an ancient demon called a <A href="/wiki/Balrog" title="Balrog">Balrog</A>. Gandalf casts the Balrog into a vast chasm, but it drags Gandalf down into the darkness with it. The rest of the Fellowship, now commanded by Aragorn, reaches <A href="/wiki/Lothl%C3%B3rien" title="Lothlórien">Lothlórien</A>, home to elves <A href="/wiki/Galadriel" title="Galadriel">Galadriel</A> and <A href="/wiki/Celeborn" title="Celeborn">Celeborn</A>. Galadriel privately informs Frodo that only he can complete the quest, and that one of his friends will try to take the Ring. Meanwhile, Saruman creates an army of <A href="/wiki/Uruk-hai" title="Uruk-hai">Uruk-hai</A> to track down and kill the Fellowship.</P>
<P>The Fellowship leaves Lothlórien by river to <A href="/wiki/Parth_Galen" class="mw-redirect" title="Parth Galen">Parth Galen</A>. Frodo wanders off and is confronted by Boromir, who tries to take the Ring in desperation. Afraid of the Ring corrupting his friends, Frodo decides to travel to Mordor alone. The Fellowship is then ambushed by the Uruk-hai. Merry and Pippin are taken captive, and Boromir is mortally wounded by the Uruk chieftain. After slaying the chieftain, Aragorn watches Boromir die peacefully. Sam follows Frodo, accompanying him to keep his promise to Gandalf to protect Frodo, while Aragorn, Legolas, and Gimli go to rescue Merry and Pippin.</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Cast">Cast</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Lord_of_the_Rings:_The_Fellowship_of_the_Ring&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: Cast">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <A href="/wiki/The_Lord_of_the_Rings_(film_series)#Cast" title="The Lord of the Rings (film series)">Cast of The Lord of the Rings film series</A></DIV>

<P>Before filming began on 11 October 1999, the principal actors trained for six weeks in sword fighting (with <A href="/wiki/Bob_Anderson_(fencer)" title="Bob Anderson (fencer)">Bob Anderson</A>), riding and boating. Jackson hoped such activities would allow the cast to bond so chemistry would be evident on screen as well as getting them used to life in <A href="/wiki/Wellington" title="Wellington">Wellington</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-cast_8-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-cast-8">[8]</A></SUP> They were also trained to pronounce Tolkien's verses properly.<SUP id="cite_ref-officialguide_9-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-officialguide-9">[9]</A></SUP> After the shoot, the nine cast members playing the Fellowship got a tattoo of the English word "nine" written in <A href="/wiki/Tengwar" title="Tengwar">Tengwar</A>, with the exception of <A href="/wiki/John_Rhys-Davies" title="John Rhys-Davies">John Rhys-Davies</A>, whose stunt double got the tattoo instead.<SUP id="cite_ref-master_10-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-master-10">[10]</A></SUP> The film is noted for having an <A href="/wiki/Ensemble_cast" title="Ensemble cast">ensemble cast</A>,<SUP id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-11">[11]</A></SUP> and some of the cast and their respective characters include:</P>
<UL>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Elijah_Wood" title="Elijah Wood">Elijah Wood</A> as <A href="/wiki/Frodo_Baggins" title="Frodo Baggins">Frodo Baggins</A>: a young <A href="/wiki/Hobbit" title="Hobbit">hobbit</A> who inherits the <A href="/wiki/One_Ring" title="One Ring">One Ring</A> from his uncle Bilbo. Wood was the first actor to be cast on 7 July 1999.<SUP id="cite_ref-12" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-12">[12]</A></SUP> Wood was a fan of the book, and he sent in an audition dressed as Frodo, reading lines from the novel.<SUP id="cite_ref-circus_13-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-circus-13">[13]</A></SUP> Wood was selected from 150 actors who auditioned,<SUP id="cite_ref-bumps_14-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-bumps-14">[14]</A></SUP> including <A href="/wiki/Jake_Gyllenhaal" title="Jake Gyllenhaal">Jake Gyllenhaal</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-15" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-15">[15]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Ian_McKellen" title="Ian McKellen">Ian McKellen</A> as <A href="/wiki/Gandalf" title="Gandalf">Gandalf the Grey</A>: an <A href="/wiki/Wizard_(Middle-earth)" title="Wizard (Middle-earth)">Istari wizard</A> and mentor to Frodo. <A href="/wiki/Sean_Connery" title="Sean Connery">Sean Connery</A> was approached for the role, but did not understand the plot,<SUP id="cite_ref-circus_13-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-circus-13">[13]</A></SUP> while <A href="/wiki/Patrick_Stewart" title="Patrick Stewart">Patrick Stewart</A> turned it down as he disliked the script.<SUP id="cite_ref-16" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-16">[16]</A></SUP> Before being cast, McKellen had to sort his schedule with <A href="/wiki/20th_Century_Fox" title="20th Century Fox">20th Century Fox</A> as there was a two-month overlap with <I><A href="/wiki/X-Men_(film)" title="X-Men (film)">X-Men</A></I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-bumps_14-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-bumps-14">[14]</A></SUP> He enjoyed playing Gandalf the Grey more than his transformed state in the next two films,<SUP id="cite_ref-master_10-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-master-10">[10]</A></SUP> and based his accent on Tolkien. Unlike his on-screen character, McKellen did not spend much time with the actors playing the Hobbits; instead he worked with their scale doubles.<SUP id="cite_ref-cast_8-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-cast-8">[8]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Sean_Astin" title="Sean Astin">Sean Astin</A> as <A href="/wiki/Samwise_Gamgee" title="Samwise Gamgee">Samwise "Sam" Gamgee</A>: a hobbit gardener and Frodo's best friend. Astin, who had recently become a father, bonded with the 18-year-old Wood in a protective manner, which mirrored Sam's relationship with Frodo.<SUP id="cite_ref-cast_8-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-cast-8">[8]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Viggo_Mortensen" title="Viggo Mortensen">Viggo Mortensen</A> as <A href="/wiki/Aragorn" title="Aragorn">Aragorn II Elessar</A>: a <A href="/wiki/D%C3%BAnedain" title="Dúnedain">Dúnedain</A> <A href="/wiki/Ranger_(Middle-earth)" title="Ranger (Middle-earth)">ranger</A>, the descendant of Isildur, and heir to <A href="/wiki/Gondor" title="Gondor">Gondor</A>'s throne. <A href="/wiki/Daniel_Day-Lewis" title="Daniel Day-Lewis">Daniel Day-Lewis</A> was offered the part at the beginning of pre-production, but turned it down.<SUP id="cite_ref-DDL_17-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-DDL-17">[17]</A></SUP> <A href="/wiki/Nicolas_Cage" title="Nicolas Cage">Nicolas Cage</A> also received an offer, declining because of "family obligations",<SUP id="cite_ref-18" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-18">[18]</A></SUP> while <A href="/wiki/Vin_Diesel" title="Vin Diesel">Vin Diesel</A>, a fan of the book, auditioned for Aragorn. <A href="/wiki/Stuart_Townsend" title="Stuart Townsend">Stuart Townsend</A> was cast in the role, before being replaced during filming when Jackson realised he was too young.<SUP id="cite_ref-circus_13-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-circus-13">[13]</A></SUP> <A href="/wiki/Russell_Crowe" title="Russell Crowe">Russell Crowe</A> was considered as a replacement, but he turned it down after taking what he thought to be a similar role in <I><A href="/wiki/Gladiator_(2000_film)" title="Gladiator (2000 film)">Gladiator</A></I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-circus_13-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-circus-13">[13]</A></SUP> Day-Lewis was offered the role for a second time, but declined again.<SUP id="cite_ref-DDL_17-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-DDL-17">[17]</A></SUP> Executive Producer <A href="/wiki/Mark_Ordesky" title="Mark Ordesky">Mark Ordesky</A> saw Mortensen in a play. Mortensen's son, a fan of the book, convinced him to take the role.<SUP id="cite_ref-cast_8-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-cast-8">[8]</A></SUP> Mortensen read the book on the plane, received a crash course lesson in fencing from Bob Anderson and began filming the scenes on Weathertop.<SUP id="cite_ref-filming_19-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-filming-19">[19]</A></SUP> Mortensen became a hit with the crew by patching up his costume<SUP id="cite_ref-costumes_20-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-costumes-20">[20]</A></SUP> and carrying his "hero" sword around with him off-camera.<SUP id="cite_ref-cast_8-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-cast-8">[8]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Billy_Boyd_(actor)" title="Billy Boyd (actor)">Billy Boyd</A> as <A href="/wiki/Peregrin_Took" title="Peregrin Took">Peregrin "Pippin" Took</A>: a hobbit who travels with the Fellowship on their journey to Mordor.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Dominic_Monaghan" title="Dominic Monaghan">Dominic Monaghan</A> as <A href="/wiki/Meriadoc_Brandybuck" title="Meriadoc Brandybuck">Meriadoc "Merry" Brandybuck</A>: a distant cousin of Frodo. Monaghan was cast as Merry after auditioning for Frodo.<SUP id="cite_ref-circus_13-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-circus-13">[13]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/John_Rhys-Davies" title="John Rhys-Davies">John Rhys-Davies</A> as <A href="/wiki/Gimli_(Middle-earth)" title="Gimli (Middle-earth)">Gimli</A>: a <A href="/wiki/Dwarf_(Middle-earth)" title="Dwarf (Middle-earth)">dwarf</A> warrior who accompanies the Fellowship to Mordor after they set out from <A href="/wiki/Rivendell" title="Rivendell">Rivendell</A> and a descendant of Durin's Folk. <A href="/wiki/Billy_Connolly" title="Billy Connolly">Billy Connolly</A>, who was considered for the part of Gimli, later portrayed <A href="/wiki/D%C3%A1in_II_Ironfoot" title="Dáin II Ironfoot">Dáin II Ironfoot</A> in <A href="/wiki/Peter_Jackson" title="Peter Jackson">Peter Jackson</A>'s <A href="/wiki/The_Hobbit_(film_series)" title="The Hobbit (film series)"><I>The Hobbit</I> film trilogy</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-circus_13-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-circus-13">[13]</A></SUP> Rhys-Davies wore heavy prosthetics to play Gimli, which limited his vision, and eventually developed <A href="/wiki/Eczema" class="mw-redirect" title="Eczema">eczema</A> around his eyes.<SUP id="cite_ref-cast_8-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-cast-8">[8]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Orlando_Bloom" title="Orlando Bloom">Orlando Bloom</A> as <A href="/wiki/Legolas" title="Legolas">Legolas Greenleaf</A>: a prince of the elves' <A href="/wiki/Mirkwood" title="Mirkwood">Woodland Realm</A> and a skilled archer. Bloom initially auditioned for <A href="/wiki/Faramir" title="Faramir">Faramir</A>, who appears in the second film, a role which went to <A href="/wiki/David_Wenham" title="David Wenham">David Wenham</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-circus_13-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-circus-13">[13]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Sean_Bean" title="Sean Bean">Sean Bean</A> as <A href="/wiki/Boromir" title="Boromir">Boromir</A>: a prince of the <A href="/wiki/Stewards_of_Gondor" title="Stewards of Gondor">Stewards of Gondor</A> who journeys with the Fellowship towards Mordor. <A href="/wiki/Bruce_Willis" title="Bruce Willis">Bruce Willis</A>, a fan of the book, expressed interest in the role, while <A href="/wiki/Liam_Neeson" title="Liam Neeson">Liam Neeson</A> was sent the script, but passed.<SUP id="cite_ref-circus_13-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-circus-13">[13]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Ian_Holm" title="Ian Holm">Ian Holm</A> as <A href="/wiki/Bilbo_Baggins" title="Bilbo Baggins">Bilbo Baggins</A>: Frodo's uncle who gives him the Ring after he decides to retire to Rivendell. Holm previously played Frodo in a <A href="/wiki/The_Lord_of_the_Rings_(1981_radio_series)" title="The Lord of the Rings (1981 radio series)">1981 radio adaption of <I>The Lord of the Rings</I></A>, and was cast as Bilbo after Jackson remembered his performance.<SUP id="cite_ref-circus_13-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-circus-13">[13]</A></SUP> <A href="/wiki/Sylvester_McCoy" title="Sylvester McCoy">Sylvester McCoy</A>, who would later play Radagast the Brown in <I><A href="/wiki/The_Hobbit_(film_series)" title="The Hobbit (film series)">The Hobbit</A></I>, was contacted about playing the role, and was kept in place as a potential Bilbo for six months before Jackson went with Holm.<SUP id="cite_ref-21" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-21">[21]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Liv_Tyler" title="Liv Tyler">Liv Tyler</A> as <A href="/wiki/Arwen" title="Arwen">Arwen Undomiel</A>: a beautiful <A href="/wiki/Elf_(Middle-earth)" title="Elf (Middle-earth)">half-elf</A> princess of Rivendell and Aragorn's lover. The filmmakers approached Tyler after seeing her performance in <I><A href="/wiki/Plunkett_%26_Macleane" title="Plunkett & Macleane">Plunkett & Macleane</A></I>, and <A href="/wiki/New_Line_Cinema" title="New Line Cinema">New Line Cinema</A> leaped at the opportunity of having one Hollywood star in the film. Actress <A href="/wiki/Helena_Bonham_Carter" title="Helena Bonham Carter">Helena Bonham Carter</A> had expressed interest in the role.<SUP id="cite_ref-circus_13-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-circus-13">[13]</A></SUP> Peter Jackson wanted to cast <A href="/wiki/Uma_Thurman" title="Uma Thurman">Uma Thurman</A> as Arwen, but Thurman pulled out due to pregnancy, Tyler came to shoot on short occasions, unlike the rest of the actors. She was one of the last actors to be cast, on 25 August 1999.<SUP id="cite_ref-22" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-22">[22]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Cate_Blanchett" title="Cate Blanchett">Cate Blanchett</A> as <A href="/wiki/Galadriel" title="Galadriel">Galadriel</A>: the elven co-ruler of <A href="/wiki/Lothl%C3%B3rien" title="Lothlórien">Lothlórien</A> alongside her husband Celeborn. Peter Jackson wanted to cast <A href="/wiki/Lucy_Lawless" title="Lucy Lawless">Lucy Lawless</A> as Galadriel, but she declined due to pregnancy.<SUP id="cite_ref-23" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-23">[23]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Christopher_Lee" title="Christopher Lee">Christopher Lee</A> as <A href="/wiki/Saruman" title="Saruman">Saruman the White</A>: the fallen head of the Istari Order who succumbs to Sauron's will through his use of the <I><A href="/wiki/Palant%C3%ADr" title="Palantír">palantír</A></I>. Lee was a major fan of the book, and read it once a year. He had also met <A href="/wiki/J._R._R._Tolkien" title="J. R. R. Tolkien">J. R. R. Tolkien</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-filming_19-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-filming-19">[19]</A></SUP> He originally auditioned for Gandalf, but was judged too old.<SUP id="cite_ref-circus_13-10" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-circus-13">[13]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Hugo_Weaving" title="Hugo Weaving">Hugo Weaving</A> as <A href="/wiki/Elrond" title="Elrond">Elrond</A>: the elven Lord of Rivendell who leads the <A href="/wiki/Council_of_Elrond" class="mw-redirect" title="Council of Elrond">Council of Elrond</A>, which ultimately decides to destroy the Ring. <A href="/wiki/David_Bowie" title="David Bowie">David Bowie</A> expressed interest in the role, but Jackson stated, "To have a famous, beloved character and a famous star colliding is slightly uncomfortable."<SUP id="cite_ref-bumps_14-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-bumps-14">[14]</A></SUP></LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Sala_Baker" title="Sala Baker">Sala Baker</A> as <A href="/wiki/Sauron" title="Sauron">Sauron</A>: the Dark Lord of <A href="/wiki/Mordor" title="Mordor">Mordor</A> and the Ring's true master who manifests as an <A href="/wiki/Eye_of_Sauron" class="mw-redirect" title="Eye of Sauron">Eye</A> after the destruction of his physical form. Originally hired as one of the several <A href="/wiki/Stunt_performer" title="Stunt performer">stunt performers</A> for the film trilogy, Baker ended up landing the role. In addition, he went on to play several Orcs as well.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Andy_Serkis" title="Andy Serkis">Andy Serkis</A> as <A href="/wiki/Gollum" title="Gollum">Gollum</A> voice and <A href="/wiki/Motion_capture" title="Motion capture">motion capture</A>: a wretched hobbit-like creature whose mind was poisoned over centuries by the Ring.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/David_Weatherley" title="David Weatherley">David Weatherley</A> as <A href="/wiki/Barliman_Butterbur" title="Barliman Butterbur">Barliman Butterbur</A>, proprietor in Bree</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Lawrence_Makoare" title="Lawrence Makoare">Lawrence Makoare</A> as <A href="/wiki/List_of_Middle-earth_Orcs#Lurtz" class="mw-redirect" title="List of Middle-earth Orcs">Lurtz</A>: the commander of Saruman's Orc forces;</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Marton_Csokas" title="Marton Csokas">Marton Csokas</A> as <A href="/wiki/Celeborn" title="Celeborn">Celeborn</A>: the elven co-ruler of <A href="/wiki/Lothl%C3%B3rien" title="Lothlórien">Lothlórien</A> alongside his wife Galadriel;</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Craig_Parker" title="Craig Parker">Craig Parker</A> as <A href="/wiki/Haldir_of_L%C3%B3rien" class="mw-redirect" title="Haldir of Lórien">Haldir</A>: the leader of the Galadhrim warriors guarding the border of Lothlórien;</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Mark_Ferguson" title="Mark Ferguson">Mark Ferguson</A> as <A href="/wiki/Gil-galad" title="Gil-galad">Ereinion Gil-galad</A>, the last Elven-King of <A href="/wiki/Noldor" title="Noldor">Noldor</A>;</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Peter_McKenzie_(actor)" title="Peter McKenzie (actor)">Peter McKenzie</A> as <A href="/wiki/Elendil" title="Elendil">Elendil the Tall</A>: the last High King of Arnor and Gondor;</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Harry_Sinclair" title="Harry Sinclair">Harry Sinclair</A> as <A href="/wiki/Isildur" title="Isildur">Isildur</A>: Elendil's son and Aragorn's ancestor who originally defeated Sauron.</LI>
<LI><A href="/wiki/Peter_Jackson" title="Peter Jackson">Peter Jackson</A> as Albert Dreary: a man of Bree.</LI>
</UL>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Comparison_with_the_source_material">Comparison with the source material</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Lord_of_the_Rings:_The_Fellowship_of_the_Ring&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Comparison with the source material">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<DIV class="thumb tright">
<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:172px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Unico_Anello.png" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b7/Unico_Anello.png/170px-Unico_Anello.png" width="170" height="147" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b7/Unico_Anello.png/255px-Unico_Anello.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b7/Unico_Anello.png/340px-Unico_Anello.png 2x" data-file-width="2240" data-file-height="1939" /></A>

The inscriptions on the Ring</DIV>

<P>Jackson, Walsh and Boyens made numerous changes to the story, for purposes of pacing and character development. Jackson said his main desire was to make a film focused primarily on Frodo and the Ring, the "backbone" of the story.<SUP id="cite_ref-Story_24-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Story-24">[24]</A></SUP> The prologue condenses Tolkien's backstory, in which The Last Alliance's seven-year siege of the <A href="/wiki/Barad-d%C3%BBr" title="Barad-dûr">Barad-dûr</A> is a single battle, where Sauron is shown to explode, though Tolkien only said his spirit flees.<SUP id="cite_ref-Letters_25-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Letters-25">[25]</A></SUP></P>
<P>Events from the book are condensed or omitted altogether at the beginning of the film. The time between Gandalf leaving the Ring to Frodo and returning to reveal its inscription, which is 17 years in the book, is compressed for timing reasons.<SUP id="cite_ref-DirectorCommentary_26-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-DirectorCommentary-26">[26]</A></SUP> Frodo also spends a few months preparing to move to Buckland, on the eastern border of the Shire. This move is omitted, and associated events, including the involvement of Merry and Pippin, are changed and combined with him setting out for Bree. Characters such as <A href="/wiki/Tom_Bombadil" title="Tom Bombadil">Tom Bombadil</A> and the incidents in the Old Forest and the Barrow Downs are left out to simplify the plot and increase the threat of the <A href="/wiki/Nazg%C3%BBl" title="Nazgûl">Ringwraiths</A>. Such sequences are left out to make time to introduce Saruman, who doesn't appear in the book until Gandalf's account at the Council of Elrond. While some characters are left out, some are referenced such as Tom, Bert, and William to show how <I>The Hobbit</I> and <I>The Lord of the Rings</I> series intertwine. Saruman's role is enhanced: he is to blame for the blizzard on Caradhras, a role taken from Sauron and/or Caradhras itself in the book. Gandalf's capture by Saruman is also expanded with a fight sequence.</P>
<P>The role of <A href="/wiki/Barliman_Butterbur" title="Barliman Butterbur">Barliman Butterbur</A> at the Prancing Pony is largely removed for time and dramatic flow. In the film Pippin is seen to identify Frodo explicitly with the phrase "why there's Baggins over there" whereas in the book Pippin is only telling the tale of Bilbo's disappearance when Strider tells Frodo to create a distraction, which he does by singing a song.</P>
<P>The events at Weathertop were also altered. The location of the fight against the Ringwraiths was changed to the ruins on top of the hill rather than a campsite at its base. When Frodo was stabbed in the book, the party spent two weeks travelling to Rivendell, but in the film this is shortened to less than a week, with Frodo's condition worsening at a commensurately greater rate. <A href="/wiki/Arwen" title="Arwen">Arwen</A> was given a greater role in the film, accompanying Frodo all the way to Rivendell, while in the book Frodo faced the Ringwraiths alone at the <A href="/wiki/Bruinen" class="mw-redirect" title="Bruinen">Ford of Bruinen</A>. The character of <A href="/wiki/Glorfindel" title="Glorfindel">Glorfindel</A> was omitted entirely and his scenes were also given to Arwen. She was tacitly credited with the river rising against the Ringwraiths, which was the work of her father <A href="/wiki/Elrond" title="Elrond">Elrond</A> with aid from <A href="/wiki/Gandalf" title="Gandalf">Gandalf</A> in the book.</P>
<P>A significant new addition is Aragorn's self-doubt, which causes him to hesitate to claim the kingship of Gondor. This element is not present in the book, where Aragorn intends to claim the throne at an appropriate time. In the book Narsil is reforged immediately when he joins the Fellowship, but this event is held over until <I><A href="/wiki/The_Lord_of_the_Rings:_The_Return_of_the_King" title="The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King">Return of the King</A></I> in film to symbolically coincide with his acceptance of his title. These elements were added because Peter Jackson believed that each character should be forced to grow or change over the course of the story.</P>
<P><A href="/wiki/Elrond" title="Elrond">Elrond</A>'s character gained an adversarial edge; he expresses doubts in the strength of Men to resist Sauron's evil after Isildur's failure to destroy the ring as depicted in the prologue. Jackson also shortens the Council of Elrond by spreading its exposition into earlier parts of the film. Elrond's counsellor, <A href="/wiki/Erestor" class="mw-redirect" title="Erestor">Erestor</A>—who suggested the Ring be given to <A href="/wiki/Tom_Bombadil" title="Tom Bombadil">Tom Bombadil</A>—was completely absent from this scene. Gimli's father, <A href="/wiki/Gl%C3%B3in" class="mw-redirect" title="Glóin">Glóin</A>, was also deemed unnecessary. In addition, the movie makes it seem by chance that the Fellowship is made of nine companions, whereas in the book Elrond suggests there be nine in the fellowship in response to the nine <A href="/wiki/Nazg%C3%BBl" title="Nazgûl">Nazgûl</A>.</P>
<P>The tone of the Moria sequence was altered. In the book, following the defeat on the Caradhras road, Gandalf advocates the Moria road against the resistance of the rest of the Fellowship (save Gimli), suggesting "there is a hope that Moria is still free...there is even a chance that Dwarves are there," though no one seems to think this likely. Frodo proposes they take a company vote, but the discovery of <A href="/wiki/Warg#J._R._R._Tolkien.27s_wargs" title="Warg">Wargs</A> on their trail forces them to accept Gandalf's proposal. They only realise the Dwarves are all dead once they reach <A href="/wiki/Balin_(Middle-earth)" title="Balin (Middle-earth)">Balin</A>'s tomb. The filmmakers chose instead for Gandalf to resist the Moria plan as a <A href="/wiki/Foreshadowing" title="Foreshadowing">foreshadowing</A> device. Gandalf says to Gimli he would prefer not to enter Moria, and Saruman is shown to be aware of Gandalf's hesitance, revealing an illustration of the Balrog in one of his books. The corpses of the dwarves are instantly shown as the Fellowship enter Moria.<SUP id="cite_ref-27" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-27">[27]</A></SUP> One detail that many critics commented upon is the fact that, in the novel, Pippin tosses a mere pebble into the well in Moria ("They then hear what sounds like a hammer tapping in the distance"), whereas in the film, he knocks an entire skeleton in ("Next, the skeleton ... falls down the well, also dragging down a chain and bucket. The noise is incredible."<SUP id="cite_ref-28" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-28">[28]</A></SUP>)<SUP id="cite_ref-29" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-29">[29]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-30" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-30">[30]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-31" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-31">[31]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-32" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-32">[32]</A></SUP></P>
<P>In terms of dramatic structure, the book simply ends; there is no climax, because Tolkien wrote the "trilogy" as a single story published in three volumes. Jackson's version incorporates the first chapter of '"The Two Towers" and makes its events, told in real time instead of flashback, simultaneous with the Breaking of the Fellowship. This finale is played as a climactic battle, into which he introduces the Uruk-hai referred to as Lurtz in the script. In the book, Boromir is unable to tell Aragorn which hobbits were kidnapped by the orcs before he dies. From there, Aragorn deduces Frodo's intentions when he notices that a boat is missing and Sam's pack is gone. In the film, Aragorn and Frodo have a scene together in which Frodo's intentions are explicitly stated.</P>
<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Production">Production</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Lord_of_the_Rings:_The_Fellowship_of_the_Ring&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Production">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>
<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Development">Development</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Lord_of_the_Rings:_The_Fellowship_of_the_Ring&action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section: Development">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>
<P><A href="/wiki/Peter_Jackson" title="Peter Jackson">Peter Jackson</A> began working with <A href="/wiki/Christian_Rivers" title="Christian Rivers">Christian Rivers</A> to <A href="/wiki/Storyboard" title="Storyboard">storyboard</A> the series in August 1997, as well as getting <A href="/wiki/Richard_Taylor_(filmmaker)" title="Richard Taylor (filmmaker)">Richard Taylor</A> and <A href="/wiki/Weta_Workshop" title="Weta Workshop">Weta Workshop</A> to begin creating his interpretation of Middle-earth.<SUP id="cite_ref-33" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-33">[33]</A></SUP> Jackson told them to make Middle-earth as plausible and believable as possible, to think of Middle-earth in a historical manner.<SUP id="cite_ref-Design_34-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Design-34">[34]</A></SUP></P>
<P>In November,<SUP id="cite_ref-Design_34-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Design-34">[34]</A></SUP> <A href="/wiki/Alan_Lee_(illustrator)" title="Alan Lee (illustrator)">Alan Lee</A> and <A href="/wiki/John_Howe_(illustrator)" title="John Howe (illustrator)">John Howe</A> became the film trilogy's primary conceptual designers, having had previous experience as illustrators for the book and various other tie-ins. Lee worked for the Art Department creating places such as <A href="/wiki/Rivendell" title="Rivendell">Rivendell</A>, <A href="/wiki/Isengard" title="Isengard">Isengard</A>, <A href="/wiki/Moria_(Middle-earth)" title="Moria (Middle-earth)">Moria</A> and <A href="/wiki/Lothl%C3%B3rien" title="Lothlórien">Lothlórien</A>, giving <A href="/wiki/Art_Nouveau" title="Art Nouveau">Art Nouveau</A> and <A href="/wiki/Geometry" title="Geometry">geometry</A> influences to the Elves and Dwarves respectively.<SUP id="cite_ref-Design_34-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Design-34">[34]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-bigature_35-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-bigature-35">[35]</A></SUP> Though Howe contributed with Bag End and the <A href="/wiki/Argonath" class="mw-redirect" title="Argonath">Argonath</A>,<SUP id="cite_ref-Design_34-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Design-34">[34]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-bigature_35-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-bigature-35">[35]</A></SUP> he focused working on armour having studied it all his life.<SUP id="cite_ref-36" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-36">[36]</A></SUP> Weta and the Art Department continued to design, with <A href="/wiki/Grant_Major" title="Grant Major">Grant Major</A> turning the Art Department's designs into architecture, and <A href="/wiki/Dan_Hennah" title="Dan Hennah">Dan Hennah</A> scouting locations.<SUP id="cite_ref-Design_34-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Design-34">[34]</A></SUP> On 1 April 1999, <A href="/wiki/Ngila_Dickson" title="Ngila Dickson">Ngila Dickson</A> joined the crew as costume designer. She and 40 seamstresses would create 19,000 costumes, 40 per version for the actor and their doubles, ageing and wearing them out for impression of age.<SUP id="cite_ref-costumes_20-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-costumes-20">[20]</A></SUP></P>
